:::{#def-finite-additivity}
#### Finite additivity

Let $\mathscr{S}$ be a [$\sigma$-algebra](#def-sigma-algebra) on a set $S$.
A [function](sets-functions.qmd#def-function) $\mu : \mathscr{S} \to [0, \infty]$,
with values in the [extended non-negative reals](sets-functions.qmd#def-extended-nonneg-reals),
is **finitely additive**
if, for every finite collection of
[pairwise disjoint](#def-pairwise-disjoint) sets $A_1, \ldots, A_n$ in $\mathscr{S}$,
the value of their union is the sum of their values:

$$\mu(A_1 \cup \cdots \cup A_n) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} \mu(A_i)$$

:::
